1. RE-CHECK RANGE. judgedRange (libs/shared/src/work/review/floor-review-start.ts) named the head sha of the NEWEST review-family run in any state as "the last verdict judged". Push B then push C before B's re-check finished: B's run was cancelled as superseded and C's re-check read only B..C, so A..B was never reviewed and that verdict feeds auto-merge. Fix: lastJudgedSha(runs) in floor-review-runs.ts = head_sha of the newest code-review/code-review-recheck run with outcome "success" (the only state where post-review posted). No posted verdict means no range, so the re-check reads the whole PR. Cost accepted: a push while the first deep review is still open now gets a whole-PR re-check.

2. REPLIES NEVER IN-THREAD. post-reply read brief.needs.comment_id, which nothing supplied (a run is started per review, which holds many line comments). Every reply was a top-level PR comment, no thread resolved. Production evidence: lore#2221 (09-28) and HALEngine#99 (09-29) replies are both top-level; no reply has run at all since the 09-30 floor move. Fix: the agent emits an optional REVIEW_THREAD_REPLIES JSON block [{comment_id, reply, resolved}] beside REVIEW_REPLY (parser in libs/shared/src/work/review/review-reply.ts); post-reply takes review_id as a need, posts each entry under its comment only when the comment belongs to that review, replies against in_reply_to_id (the thread's first comment; GitHub accepts a reply only there; ReviewComment gained in_reply_to_id), resolves only threads marked resolved from one listing, folds a stray or GitHub-refused reply into the general comment (so a refused thread does not fail the visit and re-run the agent), and uses a per-comment marker lore-reply-run: visit/iteration/commentId for redelivery.

3. REPLY PROMPT PROMISED MISSING INPUTS. ORG CONVENTION: WIRE RULES BY HAND, NEVER configs.recommended. Both lore and bowman-ui enumerate each rule explicitly. bowman-ui states the reason: "wired by hand rather than through its preset so an upstream addition never switches itself on" — with --max-warnings 0 a preset turns `npm update` into a red build nobody asked for. HAL first used the preset and was rewritten.

THE DEFECT A PRESET HID: re-lint/no-forwarding-class is type-aware and INERT without parserOptions.projectService (or projectService/tsconfigRootDir). It sat at `error` in HAL and could not fire on any input; every run passed. lore sets projectService:true; bowman-ui leaves it inert but DOCUMENTS that. Always pair it with type info or don't wire it.

CANARIES ARE THE ORG CONVENTION FOR THIS. lore: tools/eslint-canaries/pkg + scripts/check-eslint-canaries.sh, lints with --no-ignore and fails if a rule stops reporting. bowman-ui: tests/fixtures/eslint-* + 4 test suites. Without one, a quiet rule is indistinguishable from clean code — which is exactly how the inert rule above survived. HAL now mirrors lore's script. Canary gotcha: no-forwarding-class needs a CONSTRUCTOR-INJECTED port (`constructor(private readonly inner: Inner) {}`) with an empty ctor body and every method forwarding 1:1 — a field initializer does NOT trip it. Also give the canary package its own tsconfig.json so projectService finds type info there.

QUEUE SHAPES DIFFER BY REPO, PICK BY THE GATE: lore parks at `warn` with counts in comments (its lint script has NO --max-warnings 0, so warn is a resting state; all its queues are now drained). bowman-ui has no queue — it adopted only rules it already passed. A repo with --max-warnings 0 AND real debt (HAL: 422 findings) needs a third shape: leave queued rules unwired and add a ratchet script that applies them on demand and fails if a count rose or hit zero.

QUEUE MEASUREMENT TRAP (cost two wrong baselines): the preset scopes rules to test files (max-expects, no-nondeterministic-tests on; max-lines-per-function, max-statements, no-magic-numbers OFF for tests). Re-enabling through one unscoped block read 32 for max-lines-per-function vs the preset's 16. Passing an outer `files` through `extends` REPLACES each extended config's globs — moved max-comment-lines 15->16 and no-magic-numbers 12->0 (rule silently off while the config still named it). Copy the preset's own files+options per queued rule, off-blocks included.

no-cross-layer-import: folderIn() requires a `<pkg>/src/` prefix, so a single-package repo with sources at <root>/src cannot be described — every file resolves to "not governed" and the rule reports 0 while looking adopted.
